name: Selective Attention
definition: The ability to concentrate on a task over a period of time without being distracted.

benchmark.name: Adversarial SQuAD
benchmark.metric: F1 (%) on the AddSent adversarial set
benchmark.human_reference: General literate adult workforce (crowdworker readers doing reading comprehension with a distractor present). This matches the human evaluation population in Jia & Liang (2017).

benchmark.name: Distracting Control Suite
benchmark.metric: episode return (0-1000 per task); no single canonical aggregate

benchmark.name: RULER
benchmark.metric: Average accuracy (%) over the 13 RULER tasks, averaged across context lengths 4K-128K
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce: people who must focus on one defined target while reading or monitoring large amounts of irrelevant or confusable material, such as clerical workers, reviewers and analysts.

benchmark.name: Vending-Bench 2
benchmark.metric: US dollars (mean final bank balance after a 365-day simulation starting from $500, averaged over 5 runs)
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: a typical adult worker, such as a small-business operator or office worker, asked to run the simulated vending business through the same email and tool interface over a long session.

benchmark.name: Vending-Bench 2
benchmark.metric: US dollars (mean final bank balance after a 365-day simulation, averaged over multiple runs)
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: typical small-business operators or office workers asked to run a long, multi-step operational task (supplier email, inventory, pricing, refunds) consistently over an extended period without drifting off task
